We anticipate that official news for Full Self-Driving will be shared in the following hours, days, and weeks, but until then, remain aware of posts with unverified statements.

Nonetheless, very exciting times.

Some of these posts and rumors have further claimed that the first thousand who sign up for Full Self-Driving will receive an invite to this program.

This is also based on a single source and entirely unvalidated and not based on any official statements from @teslaeurope.

There have been screenshots circulating of supposed new @teslaeurope vehicle owners across Europe being informed about an Early Access Program for Full Self-Driving starting Sunday.

As far as our research has found, these screenshots are doctored and based on false information.

While experiences are typically subjective in nature, we've reiterated on multiple occasions that Tesla has continued to update the V12.6.4 model several times since its launch.

While these changes are typically minor or simply new weights, 8.6 changes much more than usual.

We've observed an influx of reports that 2026.8.6 included relaxed driver monitoring among other Full Self-Driving improvements for HW3 Tesla vehicles.

While many have felt this was subjective, we now have more proof that real changes (and improvements) were made in this update.

nitter.net/teslaeurope/status/203…


Tesla Europe, Middle East & Africa (@teslaeurope)

Together with RDW, we have officially completed the final vehicle testing phase for Full Self-Driving (Supervised) and have submitted all documentation required for the UN R-171 approval + Article 39 exemptions. The RDW team is now reviewing the documentation and test results package internally. They have communicated the expected approval for Netherlands date of 4/10, shifting from 3/20 previously and we look forward to successful completion of this cooperation. 

Following the Netherlands’ approval, European countries will be able to recognize this approval nationally. We are anticipating a possible EU-wide approval during the summer.

Over the past 18 months, this approval has involved a series of intense documentation, development, testing, research & audits. Including but certainly not limited to:

– 1,600,000+ km of FSD (Supervised) testing on EU roads
– 13,000+ customer sales ride-alongs
– 4,500+ track test scenario executions
– Thousands of pages of written documentation for 400+ compliance requirements
– Dozens of research studies into safety performance/results

We're extremely proud of the work conducted with the RDW team up until this point.

We very much look forward to the approval in April, and sharing FSD (Supervised) with our patient EU customers!



— https://nitter.net/teslaeurope/status/2034872940542800361#m

It is important to note that while Full Self-Driving (Supervised) was capable of generalized driving in unsupported regions, the software was not designed to respect many region-oriented traffic laws, traffic lights, and more.

Even supervised, this poses some safety risks.

In response to unauthorized devices activating Full Self-Driving (Supervised) in unsupported regions, @Tesla has remotely disabled some driver assistance functions on customer vehicles.

The company has communicated that some features will be restored in a future update.

Some encouraging first impressions of Tesla's latest Full Self-Driving V14.3.

Notably, speed profiles may have been refined to reduce speeding and improve overall smoothness.


Roger Kappler (@roger_kappler)

FSD 14.3 initial thoughts:

- Speed profiles seem to have been toned down, i.e. not speeding as much
- Very smooth driving overall
- Parking spot is definitely selected quicker and more decisive than before
- Tested one school parking lot, ignored handicapped parking spots (great), but happily parked in "Reserved for Principal" spot.
- Stop sign behavior feels a tad quicker (not waiting so long after coming to a complete stop)
- Blinker is activated later than previous versions (good)
- Havent seen the "P" icon to indicate the selected parking spot yet.
- Mini-braking for dancing leaves on road (might be a side-effect of "small animal detection". Certainly reminded me of early 14.2 releases...

Again, very early, so more to come...

"You have to perfect parking before you roll this out."  – @wholemars is in agreement with our viewpoint.

Let's talk about Banish. 👋

"Banish" is @Tesla's complete end-to-end parking solution: you're dropped off at your destination, exit the vehicle, and it drives away to park. When it's time to leave, the vehicle finds its way back to you in all conditions.

We've received a few dozen replies and DMs inquiring about why Banish is missing from Full Self-Driving V14.3. We believe Tesla is close, but is waiting to see how this update's improvements perform before considering releasing Banish to customers.

For Tesla to release Banish, parking has to be perfect. 

You need to have the confidence that your vehicle will efficiently and safely select an appropriate parking spot. It has to navigate all lane types to avoid blocking other drivers and ADA spots (if applicable to you).

Full Self-Driving V14.3, released today, includes two details about parking improvements:

1️⃣ Increased decisiveness of parking spot selection and maneuvering.
2️⃣ Improved parking location pin prediction, now shown on a map with a P icon.

These two improvements are paramount to further improving end-to-end parking, and we expect Tesla will analyze data and experiences in the coming weeks to determine an appropriate release timeline.

We give a rough timeline of May to June for the initial Banish release. We'll re-evaluathesete this projections and timelines for the Banish release once we've observed the improvements in today's release.
